classification.difficultyReason: Identify the half-chord right triangle and subtract its height from the pipe radius.

content.prompt:
A cylindrical pipe with a radius of 12.5 cm is filled with water to a depth, $d$ cm, as shown.

The surface of the water has a width of 20 cm.

What is the depth of the water in the pipe?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, circular pipe cross-section below the stem
spec.description: Circular pipe with a horizontal water-surface chord below its centre, a labelled radius, perpendicular centre-to-chord segment, matching double ticks, water depth dimension and caption.
spec.mathematics: Radius 12.5 cm; chord width 20 cm; half-width 10 cm. The centre-to-chord distance is 7.5 cm and the lower water segment has depth 5 cm. Drawing coordinates use a uniform factor of 1/5.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown d are visible; calculated lengths are absent.

answer.short: $5\text{ cm}$. Centre-to-water distance $=\sqrt{12.5^2-10^2}=7.5\text{ cm}$; subtract from the radius.
answer.worked:
Half the water-surface width is $20\div2=10\text{ cm}$.

Let $h$ be the distance from the centre to the water surface.

$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{12.5^2-10^2}\\h&=7.5\text{ cm}\\d&=12.5-7.5\\d&=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
